qualitative_findings.cot_excerpt:
Analysis:
- chunk-0026 (A's volunteer) is the new commitment. chunk-0027-0031 add no new commitments, conflicts, or central references beyond confirming agreement (B: "Fine", "Yep"; C: "Yeah, right") and A's deadline ("by end of week").

qualitative_findings.assessment: The continuation calls old 0026 the new commitment and its final JSON repeats the old volunteering entry without the new deadline. It stops at EOS without closing the thinking block. The short 389-token output is not a successful efficiency improvement.

qualitative_findings.status: Mixed: deadline correct, date inference unsafe

qualitative_findings.assessment: The control also recovers A’s end-of-week commitment, so the retained-history case does not prove a quality advantage. review.content_conclusion: The single-round run is complete but fabricates transcript quotations. The conditioned commitment update captures A’s new deadline, yet the transcript-only control also does so. Literal continuation is inconsistent: one case omits the deadline and never closes its thinking block; the other closes but mislabels evidence and upgrades a proposal to a commitment. Both history variants drift in the deadline sample. These raw traces are diagnostic evidence, not reliable distillation supervision.
review.structured_note_failure: All four deadline outputs (calls 6–9) contain source/citation metadata but no proposition text in their nonempty items. review.content_review_scope: All final-channel outputs and eight selected private-thinking passages; no full-trace or distribution-wide usefulness pass.
